title: Cloudflare Workers Accept Inbound TCP, with gRPC the First Protocol on Top
gist: Cloudflare Workers can now accept inbound TCP connections after eight years of HTTP-only limits, with gRPC as the first protocol built on top, but the gRPC support is a translation layer (gRPC-web under the hood) gated in private beta, and Cloudflare's own admission that it doesn't use gRPC internally suggests the feature is less mature than its marketing implies.

insights.claim: Cloudflare Workers can now accept inbound TCP connections via a new connect(socket) handler, ending an eight-year restriction dating to the platform's 2017 launch under which a Worker could only act as an HTTP server, even though it could already open outbound sockets to databases or services.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Removes a long-standing architectural constraint on Workers, opening the platform to workload categories (databases, message brokers, custom protocols) it previously could not serve at all.
insights.quote: Since the platform launched in 2017, a Worker could open outbound sockets to a database or a service, but it could only be a server for HTTP.

insights.claim: The connect(socket) handler routes inbound raw sockets to a Worker through Spectrum, Cloudflare's existing ingress proxy for non-HTTP traffic; a Worker can read/write the socket directly, hand it to another Worker, or pass it to a Durable Object, which can forward it further to a Container via getTcpPort() for full-duplex communication with any unmodified TCP-based program in any language, including a demonstrated Go gRPC echo server and Python socketserver.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: The Worker-to-Durable-Object-to-Container path is the only route that gets full-duplex arbitrary-protocol support, so architects needing true bidirectional streaming must design around Containers, not Workers alone.
insights.quote: this opens the door to full-duplex communication between client and server running any program, in any language, for any TCP-based protocol.
insights.locator: paragraph on connect(socket) and Durable Object/Container path

insights.claim: Workers alone (without a Container) can serve unary and server-streaming gRPC and call external gRPC servers, but not bidirectional streaming gRPC, because the mechanism is a translation layer -- developer code uses gRPC-web and Cloudflare converts incoming gRPC to gRPC-web and outgoing gRPC-web back to gRPC -- rather than native gRPC support.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Teams needing full bidirectional gRPC streaming directly on Workers (not via a Container) cannot get it from this release, which narrows the feature's applicability versus a 'gRPC at the edge' framing.

themes.theme: The HTTP/2 framing constraint behind the translation design

insights.claim: Workers cannot natively expose gRPC streaming because gRPC depends on HTTP/2's frame-level stream-ID control for streaming, cancellation, flow control, and trailers, and web-platform APIs like fetch() do not expose that level of control -- the same limitation browsers face, which is the original reason gRPC-web exists.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Explains the platform-level technical ceiling on this feature: as long as Workers run on fetch()-style web APIs rather than raw HTTP/2 frame access, true native gRPC on Workers (without a Container) is architecturally blocked, not just a near-term gap.
insights.quote: HTTP/2 splits requests into frames carrying stream IDs, and gRPC depends on that stream-level control for streaming, cancellation, flow control, and trailers. Web platform APIs like fetch() do not expose it.

insights.claim: Cloudflare has been converting gRPC traffic to HTTP/1.1 inside its reverse proxy since 2020 so that WAF rules and Bot Management could inspect gRPC messages, meaning the new inbound gRPC capability builds on a multi-year-old internal translation practice rather than new technology built from scratch.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: The underlying gRPC-translation plumbing is mature and production-tested since 2020 even if the new Worker-facing feature itself is brand new, which is a useful distinction when assessing implementation risk.

insights.claim: A commenter, Sebastian Buzdugan, publicly questioned whether Workers expose enough backpressure control for gRPC streams and noted that streaming edge cases are what actually determine whether an implementation holds up in production, a question the announcement post does not address.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Backpressure handling under load is an unresolved open question flagged by a practitioner, which is exactly the kind of production edge case that determines whether early adopters hit reliability problems.

themes.theme: Cloudflare's candid admission signals limited maturity

insights.claim: Cloudflare explicitly states it does not use gRPC internally, relying instead on Cap'n Proto, Cap'n Web, and its own JavaScript-native RPC system built into Workers, and says it always aims to be using its own shipped technology -- an unusually candid vendor admission that its own gRPC feature is not yet dogfooded.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A vendor admitting it doesn't use its own new feature internally is a maturity red flag worth weighing before committing production workloads to it, regardless of the feature's technical promise.
insights.quote: At Cloudflare, we use Cap'n Proto and Cap'n Web and the JavaScript-native RPC system that is built into Cloudflare Workers instead of gRPC. And when we ship things, we always aim to be using them ourselves.
insights.locator: paragraph on Cloudflare not using gRPC internally

insights.claim: The author's own analysis is that Cloudflare's choice to launch gRPC support only as a private beta -- working with a smaller set of gRPC developers first before general availability -- should be read by evaluating teams as a signal about the feature's maturity, not as corporate modesty.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Direct guidance for platform teams: treat this as an unproven, early-stage capability rather than a production-ready GA feature, regardless of how the announcement is framed.
insights.quote: Teams evaluating this should read it as a signal about maturity rather than as modesty.
insights.locator: paragraph on why this is private beta

insights.claim: Everything in Cloudflare's announcement post is gated behind a private-beta signup form, yet Cloudflare's own social media copy claimed gRPC support 'is now available' and described serving gRPC natively at the edge without translation layers -- a discrepancy the author explicitly flags as readers arriving from that social copy finding a narrower release than advertised.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A concrete example of vendor marketing overstating a feature's availability and technical nature (calling a translation layer 'native') versus what the technical documentation actually supports -- a pattern worth watching in future Cloudflare and competitor announcements.
insights.quote: Readers arriving from that will find a narrower release than advertised.
insights.locator: closing paragraph on private beta vs. social media claims

themes.theme: Strategic implications beyond the voice-AI framing

insights.claim: The author argues the announcement's framing around voice AI (low latency, persistent bidirectional client-model connections, launched during Agents Week) understates the broader significance: removing Workers' eight-year HTTP-only restriction opens entire categories of workloads previously ruled out, including message brokers, database proxies, and custom binary protocols.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Investors and platform architects should evaluate this capability on its general-purpose TCP-serving potential, not just the narrower voice-AI use case Cloudflare chose to lead with.
insights.quote: The capability underneath is broader than that framing suggests.

insights.claim: Passing a raw socket from Worker to Durable Object to Container turns the Cloudflare edge into a termination point for arbitrary TCP traffic with JavaScript-based routing logic ahead of it, giving a Worker the same 'decide before forwarding' position as an API gateway, but applied to raw sockets instead of HTTP requests -- though the announcement does not cover what inspection or policy a Worker can actually apply to a socket in that position.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: If Cloudflare later exposes deep inspection/policy hooks on raw sockets, Workers could become a general-purpose TCP-layer gateway/firewall product, a potential expansion path to watch for competitive positioning against traditional network appliances.
insights.locator: paragraph on routing position and API-gateway analogy

insights.claim: The MCP 2026-07-28 specification added gRPC as an optional transport alongside HTTP, and developers reacting to that release noted that much of agent infrastructure amounts to rediscovering remote-procedure-call conventions that predate it -- meaning a Google protocol released nearly ten years ago keeps resurfacing as the default answer for machine-to-machine traffic even in systems designed around HTTP.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: gRPC's re-emergence as MCP's machine-to-machine transport of choice suggests infrastructure vendors serving the agentic-AI stack (Cloudflare included) will keep needing to support it, reinforcing the strategic case for edge gRPC support despite its current rough edges.
insights.quote: A protocol Google released nearly ten years ago keeps arriving as the answer for machine-to-machine traffic, including in systems designed around HTTP.

insights.claim: Cloudflare says UDP-based protocols are next after gRPC, indicating inbound TCP and gRPC support is the first phase of a broader planned expansion of Workers' non-HTTP networking capabilities.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Signals a multi-protocol roadmap (TCP now, UDP next) for Workers, relevant for anyone assessing Cloudflare's long-term ambitions to be a general-purpose edge compute platform rather than an HTTP-only CDN/serverless product.
insights.quote: Cloudflare says UDP-based protocols are next.
